items.followUp: Define biology and name one method used to study living things.

rubric.why: Science is concerned with knowledge or study of the natural world.
rubric.description: Identifies science as knowledge or the study of nature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing science as knowledge or the study of the natural world.

rubric.why: Scientific knowledge is obtained through observation and experimentation.
rubric.description: Mentions observation and experiments as ways of gaining scientific knowledge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for referring to observation and experimentation.

modelAnswer: Science is the systematic study of the natural world.
It builds knowledge through observation and experiments.

items.followUp: Write two ways biodiversity benefits people or ecosystems.

rubric.why: Biodiversity provides useful resources and services to people.
rubric.description: Gives one benefit of biodiversity, such as food, medicines, raw materials, oxygen or pollination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid benefit.

rubric.why: Biodiversity supports ecosystem functioning and stability.
rubric.description: Gives a second valid benefit, such as maintaining ecosystem balance or supporting nutrient cycling.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for another valid benefit.

modelAnswer: Biodiversity provides useful resources such as food and medicines.
It helps maintain balanced and stable ecosystems.

items.followUp: Give two differences between fungi and animals.

rubric.why: Fungal cell walls contain chitin, whereas plant cell walls contain cellulose.
rubric.description: Distinguishes their cell walls: fungi have chitin; plants have cellulose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct cell-wall difference.

rubric.why: Fungi lack chlorophyll and obtain food heterotrophically, unlike plants which usually photosynthesize.
rubric.description: States that fungi do not photosynthesize and obtain food heterotrophically.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct mode-of-nutrition difference.

modelAnswer: Fungi have cell walls made of chitin, while plant cell walls are made of cellulose.
Fungi lack chlorophyll and obtain food heterotrophically, while plants generally make food by photosynthesis.

items.followUp: What is apoptosis, and what role does it play in development?

rubric.why: Apoptosis is the regulated, programmed death of a cell.
rubric.description: Defines apoptosis as programmed or controlled cell death.

rubric.why: Apoptosis removes unwanted or damaged cells and contributes to normal development and tissue maintenance.
rubric.description: States a valid importance, such as removing damaged or unneeded cells or helping development.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid role.

modelAnswer: Apoptosis is programmed, controlled cell death.
It removes damaged or unneeded cells and helps in normal development and tissue maintenance.

items.followUp: What do the symbols 2n and n represent in cell biology?

rubric.why: A diploid cell has two sets of chromosomes.
rubric.description: Defines diploid as having two sets of chromosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the diploid description.

rubric.why: A haploid cell has one set of chromosomes.
rubric.description: Defines haploid as having one set of chromosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the haploid description.

modelAnswer: A diploid cell has two sets of chromosomes and is represented by 2n.
A haploid cell has one set of chromosomes and is represented by n.

items.followUp: What happens to the reaction rate when all enzyme active sites are occupied by substrate?

rubric.why: Saturation occurs when substrate occupies all available enzyme active sites.
rubric.description: Identifies saturation as the state in which all active sites are occupied by substrate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the occupied active sites.

rubric.why: At saturation, the reaction rate is at its maximum and additional substrate does not increase it.
rubric.description: States the effect of saturation on reaction rate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the rate is maximal or will not increase further.

modelAnswer: The state in which substrate occupies all the enzyme's active sites is called saturation.
At saturation, the reaction rate is maximum and does not increase further by adding more substrate.

items.followUp: Name the scientist who proposed the lock-and-key model of enzyme action.

rubric.why: Daniel Koshland proposed the induced-fit model.
rubric.description: Names Daniel Koshland as the proposer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct scientist's name.

rubric.why: The induced-fit model was proposed in 1958.
rubric.description: Gives the year the model was proposed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct year.

modelAnswer: Daniel Koshland proposed the induced-fit model.

items.followUp: State one use of enzymes in the textile industry.

rubric.why: Enzymes are used to remove ink during the recycling of paper.
rubric.description: Identifies enzymatic de-inking of recycled paper.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes help remove ink from paper.

rubric.why: Enzymes also aid paper processing, recycling, bleaching or improvement of paper quality.
rubric.description: Gives another valid paper-industry use of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one additional valid use.

modelAnswer: Enzymes such as cellulases are used to remove ink from recycled paper.
They also help in paper processing and can improve the quality of the paper.
